name: [Katagami] People cannot sign in
message:
Five or more sign-in attempts failed in the last hour, excluding the ones where the person declined the Google consent screen (@reason:consent), which is a choice and not a fault.

The reasons that matter here:
  provider — Google returned server_error, temporarily_unavailable, or a policy block; that is an outage, not a choice
  state — the callback arrived with a code but no matching cookie; usually a cookie or redirect-URI problem
  google — the token exchange with Google failed; check client credentials
  session — our own session signing failed; that is our bug, not Google's

Every one of these is a person who wanted an account and did not get one.

Logs: https://app.datadoghq.com/logs?query=service%3Akatagami-server%20env%3Aproduction%20%40evt%3Aauth_login_failed

Before treating a spike as an outage, check it is not forged: reason:state is
mintable by anyone who GETs this callback with a `code` parameter and no
account, because a missing cookie IS the failure that reason reports. A
provider spike is much harder to fake — it needs our own httpOnly state cookie
— so weight that one heavier, and look at whether the events cluster on one IP.

A Workspace admin blocking the app also comes back as access_denied, so it
files as consent and this alert will not see it. The redirect carries nothing
that separates that from a person clicking Cancel.
